residency.test: Resident if present 182 days or more in the financial year, or 60 days in the year plus 365 days across the four preceding years. The 60-day test extends to 182 days for citizens leaving for employment abroad.
residency.rnor: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident status applies if you were non-resident in nine of the ten preceding years, or present 729 days or less in the preceding seven. RNORs are not taxed on foreign income.
residency.deemed_resident: An Indian citizen with Indian income above 1,500,000 who is not tax resident anywhere else is deemed resident and taxed as RNOR.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for ordinarily resident individuals. The financial year runs 1 April to 31 March.

headline.new_regime: the default since 2023-24: no exemptions, lower rates, nil tax up to 1,200,000 of income after rebate
headline.old_regime: still available by election, with HRA, 80C and other deductions but higher rates
headline.surcharge: 10% to 25% on high incomes, plus a 4% health and education cess on the whole liability
headline.standard_deduction: 75,000 for salaried taxpayers under the new regime

credits.name: Rebate under section 87A
credits.note: makes income up to 1,200,000 effectively tax free under the new regime, with marginal relief just above the threshold

surcharges.name: Surcharge on high income
surcharges.note: 10% of tax above 5,000,000, 15% above 10,000,000, 25% above 20,000,000 under the new regime; apply manually - marginal relief caps the increase

employee.name: Employees' Provident Fund
employee.note: 12% of basic salary; the statutory wage ceiling is 15,000 a month but many employers contribute on full basic pay

employer.name: Employees' State Insurance
employer.note: applies where monthly wages are 21,000 or less

capital_gains.listed_equity_short_term: 20% where held 12 months or less (raised from 15% in July 2024)
capital_gains.listed_equity_long_term: 12.5% above an annual exemption of 125,000, where held more than 12 months
capital_gains.other_assets_long_term: 12.5% without indexation, held more than 24 months; resident individuals may use the 20% with indexation option for property bought before 23 July 2024
capital_gains.property: exemption available under sections 54 and 54F where proceeds are reinvested in residential property

quirks: The new regime is the default. If the old regime is better for you - typically where you claim house rent allowance, home loan interest and the full 150,000 under section 80C - you must actively elect it, and salaried taxpayers can switch each year.
The financial year runs 1 April to 31 March, and the return is filed for the 'assessment year' that follows. Getting these two labels mixed up is the most common filing error.
Form 26AS and the Annual Information Statement show everything the tax department already knows about your income. Reconciling against them before filing prevents almost all notices.
Advance tax is due in four instalments if your liability exceeds 10,000, and interest under sections 234B and 234C accrues automatically if you underpay.

The Liberalised Remittance Scheme applies a 20% tax collected at source on most foreign remittances above 1,000,000 a year, which is creditable against your final liability but is a real cash flow cost.

reporting.authority: Income Tax Department, Central Board of Direct Taxes
reporting.who_must_file: Anyone with income above the basic exemption limit before deductions, anyone with foreign assets or signing authority over a foreign account, and anyone meeting the high-value transaction criteria such as large deposits, foreign travel spending or electricity bills.

deadlines.what: Return for financial year 2025-26 for individuals not subject to audit
Return where a tax audit is required
Belated or revised return, with a late fee
Advance tax instalments at 15%, 45%, 75% and 100% cumulative
Employers issue Form 16 for the preceding financial year

forms.name: Salary, one house property and other income up to 5,000,000
Capital gains, more than one property, or foreign assets
Employer certificate of salary paid and tax deducted
Consolidated tax credit statement and Annual Information Statement
Election to opt out of the new tax regime

documents_to_collect: PAN and Aadhaar, which must be linked
Form 26AS and the Annual Information Statement, downloaded from the portal
Bank interest certificates and Form 16A for other tax deducted at source
Capital gains statements from brokers and mutual funds
Rent receipts and landlord PAN if claiming house rent allowance under the old regime
Details of all foreign assets and foreign bank accounts - Schedule FA is mandatory and heavily penalised

penalties.late_filing_fee: 5,000 under section 234F, reduced to 1,000 where total income is 500,000 or less
penalties.interest: 1% a month under section 234A for late filing, 234B and 234C for advance tax shortfalls
penalties.underreporting: 50% of the tax on underreported income, 200% where it is misreported
penalties.foreign_assets: penalties of 1,000,000 under the Black Money Act for failing to report foreign assets, regardless of the amount involved

warnings: Surcharge on income above 5,000,000 is NOT applied - the entry carries a zero rate so it never double-counts, which also means it does not appear in the output. Add 10%, 15% or 25% manually, with marginal relief.
The old regime with its deductions (80C, 80D, HRA, home loan interest) is not modelled. For taxpayers with significant deductions it can produce a lower result.
Provident fund is charged here on the full salary up to a proxy ceiling; in practice it is charged on basic pay, which is typically 40% to 50% of the total.
